newsitem.title: BRAZIL: LatAm shrs seen firming this week on local factors.
newsitem.headline: LatAm shrs seen firming this week on local factors.

text.p: Stocks in most Latin American bourses are seen firming this week on local factors, including lower interest rates in Venezuela and speculative buying ahead of third quarter corporate earnings in Mexico, analysts said.
Brazilian equities are seen as an exception, as sluggishness is expected to continue ahead of the first round of the country's municipal elections on Thursday, they added.
Last week, Brazil's share prices fell 1.9 percent, closing Friday at 64,589 points amid a lack of market-moving news and investor caution before the polls.
Despite chances of occasional technical corrections, the vertical rise in Caracas stocks looks set to continue, dealers said.

Plentiful liquidity continues to push down domestic rates, so that the rise in equity prices and market expectations -- egged-on by telephone company Cantv's slated November share offering -- show no signs of abating, they noted.
"The general trend remains up, although stocks could dip any time this week on a bout of profit-taking," said Bancaracas broker Ricardo Larrazabal.
Last week, the market's 19-share index rose 8.5 percent, closing Friday at 5,450.52 points in its sixth consecutive record-breaking session.

Scattered profit-taking could also cut Argentine stocks' gains, but the bullish mood continues. Argentine stocks are expected to keep their firm tone, although there could be some scattered profit-taking, dealers said.
"The market looks pretty healthy and should be able to overcome resistance levels if volume grows," said Miguel Daneri, from Boston Securities.
Traders also said the market could be underpinned by a labor reform package which President Carlos Menem has said may be heading for Congress this week.

The bolsa's blue-chip Merval index closed last week with a rise of 1.4 percent, ending Friday at 555.65. However, daily turnover slowed due to a Jewish holiday, tension ahead of an U.S. Federal Reserve meeting and a 36-hour general strike which started midday Thursday.

In Mexico, equities are likely to benefit from speculative demand ahead of third quarter corporate results, which would keep the market away from its technical resistance currently at 3,200 points, traders said.
Analysts said the market's current levels are seen attractive for selective buying. Last week, Mexico's IPC index fell 2.45 percent.
Chilean stocks are also seen moving on expected news of third quarter corporate results, which are starting to filter into the market.
Analysts said Chilean investors would also be paying close attention to events in Argentina, where several Chilean leading companies have heavy investments.
"Even though no more than 20 percent of any of these companies' assets are at stake, investors will sell if there are more jitters in Argentina," said Karl Kluever, general manager of Copinvest.
The selective IPSA index ended 0.75 percent higher last week at 98.95 points.
